knowledge.text: The actual diff replaced the prior 'search each surface/container exactly once before revisiting' principle with a one-pass order that checks plausible open surfaces before closed containers and advances through location families without immediate backtracking. In three current missing-target pairs, Candidate took an open surface while Parent took a closed drawer at the same prior state, and Candidate reached the target earlier: train:0007 (put a pencil in desk), after desk 1 Parent went to drawer 1 (P8:2) while Candidate went to shelf 1 (Q8:2), took pencil 3 (Q8:3), and moved it to desk 1 (Q8:5), finishing 5 steps versus Parent's 12 (P8:12); train:0004 (look at statue under the desklamp), after shelf 9 Parent went to drawer 1 (P5:10) while Candidate went to dresser 1 (Q5:10), took statue 1 (Q5:11), and used the desklamp (Q5:12), finishing 12 versus Parent's 19 (P5:19); train:0006 (put some newspaper on sofa), after sidetable 1 Parent went to drawer 1 (P7:9) while Candidate went to tvstand 1 (Q7:9), took newspaper 1 (Q7:10), and placed it on sofa 1 (Q7:12), finishing 12 versus Parent's 29 (P7:29). These paired divergences are consistent with the surface-first clause, but because the edit changed several search rules and object placements differed, the step reductions cannot be attributed to that clause alone.

The intended one-pass, non-cycling search was not universally effective. In train:0005 (put a cellphone in shelf), Candidate did initially move to open surfaces bed 1 and shelves 1-2 before opening drawers (Q6:2, Q6:3, Q6:4, Q6:5), but then repeatedly cycled among desk 1, bed 1, shelf 1, shelf 2, and drawers 1-6 (returning to drawer 1 at Q6:24 and to desk 1 at Q6:32, Q6:41, Q6:50), never visited sidetable 1 in the recorded run, and ended at the 50-step limit without success. Parent succeeded in 46 steps by reaching sidetable 1 (P6:43), taking cellphone 1 (P6:44), and placing it on shelf 2 (P6:46). This is a material Parent-success/Candidate-step-limit difference under the joint edit; the step-limit outcome leaves open whether Candidate could later have found the object, and the trajectory does not isolate which edited clause caused the omission, but it shows the new guidance did not ensure coverage or prevent repeated family cycling in this missing-target case.

Preserved capabilities under the edit: in current pairs where the required object was visible at the first relevant location, Candidate still took it immediately and delivered/used it with the same short successful trajectory as Parent. train:0000 both 4 steps (P1:2/Q1:2 take alarmclock 2; P1:4/Q1:4 use desklamp); train:0001 both 4 steps (P2:2/Q2:2 take cd 1; P2:4/Q2:4 use desklamp); train:0003 both 4 steps (P4:2/Q4:2 take pillow 1; P4:4/Q4:4 use desklamp); train:0008 both 4 steps (P9:2/Q9:2 take soapbar 2; P9:4/Q9:4 move to garbagecan); train:0009 both 4 steps (P10:2/Q10:2 take statue 1; P10:4/Q10:4 move to coffeetable). In train:0002 both sides took cd 1 at step 2 and completed in 7 identical steps (P3:2/Q3:2; P3:7/Q3:7), though they continued searching for the desklamp after acquisition. These cases show no disruption of visible-object acquisition or delivery, but they do not exercise missing-target search.
